steps.title: The Open
steps.content:
Hi, this is {{caller_name}} with {{provider_name}}'s office. Is {{contact_first_name}} available, please?

Hi {{contact_first_name}}. You reached out {{submitted_ago}} about our {{offer_name}}. {{asked_by_provider}} Do you have a quick minute?

steps.title: “I don’t remember that”
Why They Didn’t Book
“I never got a call back”
steps.content:
I'm sorry about that, {{contact_first_name}}. That's on us, and I'm glad I caught you now. You're still interested in getting that looked at, right?

(Let them answer.)

steps.title: “I got busy”
steps.content:
Totally understand. Life fills up fast. The good news is the first visit is quick, and we work around your schedule. Is what you reached out about still bothering you?

(Let them answer.)

steps.title: “It was the cost”
steps.content:
That's fair, and I'm glad you said so. {{price_line}} That covers the first visit, and there's no commitment past it. Is the cost the only thing that held you back?

(Let them answer. If they name another reason, tap that button.)

steps.title: “I’m still deciding”
steps.content:
That makes sense. Most people want to know a bit more before they book. Can I ask what you're weighing?

(Let them answer. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: “I booked somewhere else”
steps.content:
Good for you for taking care of it. How's it going so far?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other office.)

If it doesn't turn out the way you hoped, we're here. Thanks for letting me know, {{contact_first_name}}.

(Add your notes and log the call as Booked elsewhere.)

steps.title: Not Interested
steps.content:
No problem at all, {{contact_first_name}}. Thanks for your time today. If anything comes up, we're here.

(Add your notes and log the call as Spoke, didn't book.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions. Is that okay?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: What Made Them Reach Out
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, tell me a bit about what made you fill out that form. What's been bothering you most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask three quick questions about {{main_concern}}. This helps us get ready for your visit.

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "Got it.")

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "I see." or "I understand.")

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. If they name an impact, reflect only what they said about work, home, or their own time. If not, you can say "Got it, thank you.")

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been going on a while, and it comes up more than once in a while. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: work, home, or your own time. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd really like to get that handled. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's exactly what the {{offer_name}} is for. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. You get everything the offer includes, and a straight answer on where things stand. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like massage, physical therapy, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all help, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what's going on with {{main_concern}}. Coming in for the {{offer_name}} gives you something real to compare against.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost or Insurance
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the price itself, or not knowing what comes after the first visit?

(Let them answer.)

{{price_line}}

The offer covers the whole first visit, and you're not signing up for anything past it. You'll hear what anything else would cost before you decide. The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get that first visit on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m worried about the time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about what comes after?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} takes a look and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that's a couple of visits. Sometimes it's more, and you'll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing you up for a long plan on the phone.

We have early and late openings, and the first visit is usually under an hour.

Could you find that time this week?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that it bothers you and you don't know why. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} was bothering you enough to fill out a form. It's had time to sort itself out on its own, and it hasn't. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Send me information”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you why {{main_concern}} keeps showing up for you. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at you, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?

steps.title: Scheduling
steps.content:
Great, {{contact_first_name}}. We have time this week on (day) and (day). Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?

(Let them answer.)

Perfect. I have (time) and (time). Which is better?

(Let them answer.)

Great, I've got you down for (day) at (time). You'll get everything in the {{offer_name}} at that visit.

(Have two days and two times ready before the call, both within 48 hours.)

(Once booked, add your notes and press the green "Booked" button below to log the call.)

steps.title: Confirm Their Requested Time
steps.content:
Hi, this is {{caller_name}} with {{provider_name}}'s office. Is {{contact_first_name}} available, please?

Hi {{contact_first_name}}. You reached out {{submitted_ago}} about our {{offer_name}}, and you asked for {{requested_time}}. I'm calling to lock that in. Does that time still work for you?

(Let them answer. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Locked In
steps.content:
Perfect. You're all set for {{requested_time}} with {{provider_name}}. You'll get everything in the {{offer_name}} at that visit. Anything I can answer before then?

(Let them answer.)

Great. We'll see you then, {{contact_first_name}}.

(Add your notes and press the green "Confirmed requested time" button below to log the call. The time is already filled in.)

steps.title: Move the Time
steps.content:
No problem at all, {{contact_first_name}}. Let's find one that works. Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?

(Let them answer.)

I have (time) and (time). Which is better?

(Let them answer. Have two days and two times ready before the call, both within 48 hours.)

Great, let's move you to (day) at (time). Does that work?

(Wait for the yes. Then tap the button below and pick the new time.)

steps.title: New Time Locked In
steps.content:
Perfect. You're all set for (day) at (time) with {{provider_name}}. You'll get everything in the {{offer_name}} at that visit. Anything I can answer before then?

(Let them answer.)

Great. We'll see you then, {{contact_first_name}}.

(Pick the new time in the "Rescheduled" button below, add your notes, and log the call.)
